newsitem.title: JAPAN: MITI says former official involved in scandal - Jiji.
newsitem.headline: MITI says former official involved in scandal - Jiji.

text.p: An internal investigation by the Trade Ministry has revealed that a former ministry official approached power utilities about buying fuel from Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd, Jiji news agency quoted Trade Minister Shinji Sato as telling parliament on Friday.
The former official is believed to have acted on behalf of an oil product wholesaler who was arrested last year on tax evasion charges, Sato was quoted as saying.

Sato, speaking to a parliamentary committee, said that out of Japan's nine utilities, two utilities, Chubu Electric Power Co Inc and Kansai Electric Power Co Inc, were approached by the former official.
Sato explained to the committee that the former ministry official has admitted to introducing Mitsubishi Oil to Kansai and Chubu Electric, Jiji said.
Separately on Friday, Mitsubishi Oil said its chairman Kikuo Yamada and vice president Masafumi Kishi are to resign from their posts effective March 31.
Mitsubishi said the resignations were not to take management responsibility for its involvement in the oil products scandal, but to take responsibility for its role in "disrupting the public".
Jiji quoted the trade minister as saying: "The talks (between the former ministry official and the two utilities) were purely on a commercial basis and do not distort (Japan's) energy policy."
The arrest of the Osaka oil dealer, Junichi Izui, prompted a ministry survey which revealed that more than 100 bureaucrats had dined, drunk or golfed with Izui.
Several senior bureaucrats were disciplined over the case.
